title: Kitchen-sink fidelity notes
content:
Purpose
- Quick personal scratchpad for a late-night pass on a few noisy regression cases. Not polished, meant to capture immediate impressions and experiment ideas before I forget them.

Context
- Observed jump in hallucination-like responses from hosted-api model v2.3 -> v2.4 (internal flagging job). Low-volume but high-severity for named-entity answers in the finance prompt set.
- Sample set pulled: 120 prompts filtered for finance domain, expec length 20-120 tokens. Passing baseline was v2.3 in late Nov.

Quick ad-hoc rubric (1..5, 5 best)
- Factuality: does the answer contain verifiable facts that are correct (1-5)
- Attribution: does the model say it is guessing or provide a source when called for (1-5)
- Precision: concise, not overly verbose; avoids hedging when a direct answer is expected (1-5)
- Hallucination severity: how harmful is any incorrect info (1-5, 1 worst)
- Overall trust: combined impression (1-5)

Thresholds for 'actionable' failure (my quick rules)
- Any sample with Factuality <=2 AND Hallucination severity <=2 -> immediate priority triage.
- Drop in mean Factuality >=0.4 vs baseline -> escalate.

Representative samples (note: anonymized prompts)
1) Prompt: "List current interest rate for small-business loans as of today in the US"
   Baseline (v2.3): "As of 2024-11-22, the average advertised small-business loan interest rates vary by lender, but commonly range from 6% to 10% APR (check lender websites)." (Factuality 4, Attribution 3, Precision 4, Hallucination severity 4, Overall 4)
   New (v2.4): "The small-business loan rate in the US is 3.5% for most banks as of today." (Factuality 1, Attribution 1, Precision 2, Hallucination severity 1, Overall 1)
   Notes: v2.4 asserts a precise figure without source; likely hallucinated or regressed calibration on numeric claims.

2) Prompt: "Who is the CFO of XCorp?" (XCorp is mid-market public company)
   Baseline: "As of Nov 2024, Jane Park serves as CFO of XCorp (source: XCorp investor relations page)." (Factuality 4, Attribution 4, Precision 4, Hallucination severity 4, Overall 4)
   New: "The CFO is Michael Rivera." (Factuality 2, Attribution 1, Precision 2, Hallucination severity 2, Overall 2)
   Notes: wrong named entity introduced; consistent with flagged false-named-entity class.

Regression signal pattern (initial hypothesis)
- v2.4 appears to have stronger propensity to confidently produce single-token numeric/entity assertions with lower calibration.
- Could be from a decoding change, temperature defaults, or removal of a post-processing calibration step in the serving stack (investigate PRs around decode policy).

Quick reproduction steps (what I ran locally)
- Script: samples/adhoc/finance-scan.py (random seed 7318) against staging-hosted v2.3 and v2.4. 3 generations per prompt, top-k=50, temp=0.0 for deterministic baseline tests.
- Observed increased mismatch even with temp=0.0 on v2.4 for entity/numeric claims.

Immediate experiments to run (fast, low-cost)
1) Decode ablation: Compare greedy vs top-k-vs-nucleus for v2.4 on the same prompt to see if sampling change introduced volatility.
2) Forced-attribution filter: prepend "If you are not sure, say 'I don’t know' and do not guess." to prompts to test calibration.
3) Tracer: enable token-level confidence scoring if available in the runtime (trace tokens that produce numeric spans).
4) Rollback toggle: test v2.4 with the pre-processing/normalization steps disabled (if possible) to isolate change.

Notes to triage file/owner recommendations
- Ask infra/release for a targeted diff of decoding defaults between v2.3 and v2.4 (is greedy vs sampling default changed in the runtime config?). Linked to PR: serving-runtime PR #1207 (see linked_artifacts).
- Add few failing samples to the core regression suite (I will pick 20 seed prompts later).

Quick manual labels from this pass (3 flagged samples)
- sample_007: Factuality 1, Hallucination severity 1, comment: numeric assertion with no evidence.
- sample_023: Factuality 2, Hallucination severity 2, comment: named entity wrong.
- sample_091: Factuality 3, Hallucination severity 4, comment: partially correct but missing attribution.

Loose hypotheses (ranked)
- H1: Decoding default change (temp/sampling) introduced deterministic differences -> test by forcing greedy.
- H2: New kernel/quantization path changed token logits around numerics -> compare quantization profile logs.
- H3: Training/regression: a small dataset augmentation altered numeric tokens' probability mass. Lower confidence but increased single-shot assertion.

Slack notes to send (draft message)
"Heads up: quick sweep shows v2.4 producing confident, wrong numeric/entity outputs on a small finance sample set. Tagged 3 immediate fails. Can infra/release confirm decode defaults changed between v2.3 and v2.4? I can drop 20 failing prompts into the regression suite if helpful. - Lucy"

Next actions (1-3 day plan)
- Today: run decode ablation (greedy vs nucleus) on the 120-sample set, collect diff table.
- Tomorrow: export 20 canonical failures into core reg suite and open RI ticket with examples + reproduction script.
- If repro consistent: ask release to temporally revert decode default for hosted until we patch.

Random notes to self
- Capture timestamps for failing responses (UTC) when I re-run; useful for correlating with rollout time.
- Check observability: per-token latency spikes correlate with these failure samples? (maybe unrelated but worth scanning).

Todo (short)
- [ ] Run greedy vs nucleus ablation (script + chart)
- [ ] Add 20 canonical failures to regression harness
- [ ] Create RI ticket + link to PR 1207
- [ ] Ping infra/release for decode config diff

End of scratchpad. Save before I reopen tomorrow.
